generators.carrier: matrices over a common finite-dimensional space
lists of P that are linear extensions

relations.statement: If x,y are adjacent in a listing and incomparable, then the ordered product of the listing equals the ordered product of the listing with x,y swapped, since A_x A_y = A_y A_x.
relations.hypotheses: x,y incomparable in P; A_x A_y = A_y A_x

relations.statement: Any two linear extensions of a finite strict poset are connected by a finite sequence of adjacent swaps of incomparable elements, each intermediate listing being a linear extension.
relations.hypotheses: P finite strict poset; both listings are linear extensions

lemmas.statement: For a finite strict poset P and matrices A_x commuting on all incomparable pairs, the ordered product is the same for all linear extensions.
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem linext_indep {n : ℕ} (P : Type) [Fintype P] (A : P → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℚ) : True := by sorry

lemmas.statement: For lists l1 l2 and matrices A_x, A_y with A_x A_y = A_y A_x, prod(l1 ++ [x,y] ++ l2) = prod(l1 ++ [y,x] ++ l2).
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem swap_lemma {n : ℕ} (A : ℕ → Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℚ) (l1 l2 : List ℕ) (x y : ℕ) (h : Commute (A x) (A y)) : ((l1 ++ [x,y] ++ l2).map A).prod = ((l1 ++ [y,x] ++ l2).map A).prod := by sorry

near_misses.claim: Two spacelike elements carrying anticommuting Pauli matrices (e.g. X and Z) give ordered products differing by a sign -1 between the two linear extensions.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Independence requires commutation on all incomparable pairs; XZ = -ZX violates it.

near_misses.claim: Swapping adjacent comparable elements preserves the product.
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: Swaps must keep the listing a linear extension, which forces the swapped pair to be incomparable.

open_obligations: No existing declarations in the SRC list concern ordered products; all generators, relations and lemmas are proposed_new.
Lean proof of the swap lemma for general n and of connectivity of linear extensions under adjacent swaps is not done.
Exact Pauli checks for the diamond and N poset are not computed.
The N poset linear extension count was not verified here.
Epstein-Glaser relation remains an analogy only.
